title: Finite = proper with finite fibres; Stacks Lemma 30.21.1
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, where $S$ is
locally Noetherian. The following are
equivalent:

1. **(1)** $f$ is
finite;
1. **(2)** $f$ is
proper with finite
fibres, in the sense of
[pqf-def-quasifinite].

(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.21.1, Tag
[02OG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OG).*)

proof.text: *(1) $\Rightarrow$ (2).* If $f$ is finite, then it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. It is quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf], and a quasi-finite morphism has finite fibres by [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres]. Thus $f$ is proper with finite fibres.

*(2) $\Rightarrow$ (1).* Assume that $f$ is proper with finite fibres. By [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $f$ is of finite type, locally of finite type, and quasi-compact. The converse implication of [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] therefore makes $f$ quasi-finite. Applying [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] to this quasi-finite morphism gives that $f$ is locally quasi-finite. Since $f$ is proper and locally quasi-finite, $f$ is finite by [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite]. The locally Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is part of the stated theorem but is not needed for this implication.
